name: Dubai
intro: Dubai is a global city and aviation hub, offering a multicultural environment and a popular, value-for-money study destination for Indian students. With international universities from the UK, Australia, Europe and the USA offering programmes in Dubai, students can explore shorter, intensive courses and, where permitted, opportunities to transfer to the parent campus.
visa: For Dubai the respective universities will file the visa application. Student visa is granted for one year and is to be renewed every year. Initially the student gets an entry permit to enter Dubai and then the visa is granted at the visa office of Dubai airport.
intakes: Dubai Universities have two major intakes: January and September.

req.label: Academics
req.value: A bachelor's degree with 50%+ and relevant prerequisite courses

req.label: Age / Gap
req.value: No age barriers and educational gaps are accepted

req.label: Documents
req.value: SOP, CV, LORs, transcripts, passport, insurance

sch.name: University based
sch.text: Upto 50% based on the student's profile

steps.title: Submit Documents
steps.text: Students must submit all required documents, preferably at least 4 weeks before the course commencement date, to allow sufficient time for processing.

steps.title: Accept offer and make payment
steps.text: Students must pay the first tuition fee instalment and visa fees as per the university's payment plan.

steps.title: Visa File Submission
steps.text: Submit documents as per check list. University will lodge visa application. Evisa issued for 90 days.

steps.title: Arrive in Dubai
steps.text: Complete formalities like medical, biometrics, insurance for Emirates ID processing.

work: Post Graduate students can legally change their student visa to work visa in case if they find an employer. The same student can continue his studies as a part time student. The classes will be from 6 PM to 9 PM or on weekends (depending upon University).

faq.a: Students in Dubai are permitted to work part-time with a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their university. They can work up to 20 hours per week and can expect to earn a minimum monthly wage ranging between 5,000 to 10,000 AED.
There is no Post-Study Work Visa in Dubai; however, if a student secures a job, they can convert the study visa to a work visa.

faq.q: Can I get the IELTS waiver option?
faq.a: IELTS waiver is possible in Dubai. Universities such as Heriot Watt University, Middlesex University, Manipal University, Global Business School, Murdoch University, De Montfort University, Regent College Dubai, University of Birmingham, UK College of Business and Computing, Dubai provide IELTS Waiver with certain criteria.

faq.q: Do I need to show funds for visa?
faq.a: There is no need for a Show Fund in Dubai. Student needs to pay the first instalment which is approximately 25% to 50% of first year tuition fees along with visa fees. Students can pay the remaining fees after reaching Dubai.
